message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water’s freezing (melting) point is slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the water phase‑diagram, the melting temperature at 10 kPa is about **–2 °C** (more precisely –2.0 °C to within a few tenths of a degree).  

So, if you cool liquid water down to roughly –2 °C while maintaining a pressure of 10 kPa, it will begin to freeze.
